messages:
oliver: FYI planning to cut the py/ts SDK publish at 16:00 PT today. primary goals: canary -> staggered -> stable, attach deprecation note for legacy sync client, and ensure server-side fallback routing in case of regressions.

maria: noted. I'll kick off the canary publish 16:00 PT, then a 30m observation window before the stable tag. smoke tests + usage sampling.

sam: +1. Can we pin the major bugfix to a known composer? i.e., publish canary as `3.4.0-canary.1` and stable `3.4.0` only after checks. Also suggest adding npm tag `canary` -> `npm publish --tag canary`.

jen: Deploy criteria: if canary fails any of the infra smoke tests (token auth, streaming, JSON schema) or user-visible error rate > 1.5% on dev traffic, we abort stable rollout and root cause. Rollback plan: yank npm/pypi tag and republish previous stable.

oliver: Good. Add this to release notes: deprecate legacy sync client (sync-api v1). Add migration link to docs and state removal planned in v4.0. Keep a short grace period note. Dev-docs, can you craft the blurb? @dev-docs-bot please.

dev-docs-bot: Draft: "Deprecation: legacy sync client (sync-api v1) — We will stop shipping this client in the v4.0 major release. Please migrate to the new async client. Migration guide: https://internal.redwood.dev/migrate-sync-to-async". I can attach to the changelog PR.

maria: Also adding a server-side compatibility flag to route requests from clients with header `x-rw-sdk-version` < 3.4.0 to the legacy-handling cluster for 72 hours after stable cut, then flip off if no issues. That lets us quickly mitigate unexpected regressions without user-side rollbacks.

sam: Important: ops needs a toggle that can be hit from the console and an automated alert if more than 0.5% of production requests hit the legacy cluster after cut. ops oncall should be in the loop.

maria: Confirmed. I'll create two toggles: `route-legacy-cluster` (manual) and `auto-fallback-on-failure` (auto, triggers if errors spike).

deploy-bot: publish job started: py-ts-sdk-canary -> 2081234600. Logs: https://ci.redwood.dev/builds/py-ts-sdk/2081234600

deploy-bot: py package uploaded to pypi as `redwood-sdk==3.4.0-canary.1` — status: success. npm package published with tag `canary` — status: success.

jen: Running smoke tests now. Patch tests: `auth smoke`, `stream smoke`, `embedding smoke`. Using canary traffic slice: 0.5% of stable traffic routed to canary.

jen: auth smoke passed. stream smoke: 1 failure (transient), rerunning. embedding smoke passed.

jen: rerun fixed stream transient. All canary smoke passed. No elevated errors in the 30m window (error rate 0.12%).

oliver: Proceed to stable cut in 10. Maria, execute stable publish and pinging (tag + update release_notes). Sam, coordinate the deprec notice in the designer portal.

maria: Executing stable publish now. Commands run: ```bash
# python publish
python -m build && twine upload dist/*
# npm publish stable
npm publish --access public
```

deploy-bot: stable publish started -> job 2081235000

deploy-bot: stable publish succeeded. pypi: `redwood-sdk==3.4.0`. npm: `@redwood/sdk@3.4.0` (tag: latest)

oliver: Pinning guidance for apps: recommend pin to `~3.4.0` for patch pulls, or `^3.4.0` if teams want minor bump safety. Add note: do not pin to `latest` for automated builds until you verify.

sam: Release notes PR: #4223 with deprecation blurb and migration link. Please review — I'll merge once docs acked.

dev-docs-bot: PR created: https://git.internal.redwood/release-notes/4223 — includes changelog, deprecation entry, and migration steps.

jen: Post-cut checklist: enable `route-legacy-cluster` manually if any client regressions appear. If error rate >1.5% or schema errors >0.3%, flip auto-fallback and page oncall.

oliver: TL;DR decisions: canary->stable cut done; deprecation note published; server-side routing in place as safety; rollback plan = yank + republish previous stable; ops toggles enabled. Good work team, monitor until EOD. :rocket:

sam: I'll watch the dashboards and update the thread if anything pops.

maria: I'll keep the auto-fallback set to enabled for 72 hours, then we'll review telemetry before turning it off.

deploy-bot: monitoring: 30m post-cut error rate 0.11%, legacy cluster usage 0.0% (as expected). Monitoring window open for 72 hours.

oliver: Thanks. I'll send a short note in #announcements once docs PR lands.
